The 11th study (Phase 3 electronic reader training study [GE067-021]) enrolled no subjects but analyzed images from the other 10 studies (not including the Japanese studies) to assess the effectiveness of an electronic program for training clinicians in the appropriate interpretation of [18F]flutemetamol PET images.

indication.text: Vizamyl is indicated for PET imaging of the brain to estimate beta amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline. A negative scan indicates sparse to no neuritic plaques and is inconsistent with a neuropathologic diagnosis of AD.

target_moa.text: Flutemetamol F 18 is a molecular imaging agent that binds to beta-amyloid plaques in the brain; the F-18 isotope produces a positron signal detected by a PET scanner. In vitro binding to postmortem human brain homogenates containing fibrillar beta-amyloid showed a dissociation constant (Kd) of 6.7 nM.

citations.quote: Vizamyl contains flutemetamol F 18, a molecular imaging agent that binds to \beta-amyloid aggregates, and is intended for use with PET imaging of the brain.

Flutemetamol F 18 binds to \beta-amyloid plaques in the brain and the F-18 isotope produces a positron signal that is detected by a PET scanner. In *in vitro* binding studies using postmortem human brain homogenates containing fibrillar \beta-amyloid, the dissociation constant (K_d) for flutemetamol was 6.7 nM.

key_safety.text: Most commonly reported adverse reactions were flushing (16; 2%), increased blood pressure (10; 1%), headache (10; 1%), nausea (8; 1%), and dizziness (8; 1%) among 761 subjects. One subject experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction with flushing, dyspnea, and chest pressure and recovered with treatment.

summary.text: Vizamyl followed the established regulatory pathway for beta-amyloid PET imaging agents (similar to florbetapir F 18/Amyvid), with no advisory committee meeting held and a pediatric study requirement waived because the disease pathophysiology occurs only in adults. Approval was based on single-arm diagnostic-performance studies using post-mortem histopathology as the truth standard.
